cases.sentence: 13-го июня в 2 часа ночи, государь, призвав к себе Балашева и прочтя ему свое письмо к Наполеону, приказал ему отвезти это письмо и лично передать ___.
cases.explain: «французскому императору» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: At two in the morning of the fourteenth of June, the Emperor, having sent for Balashëv and read him his letter to Napoleon, ordered him to take it and hand it personally to the French Emperor. When dispatching Balashëv, the Emperor repeated to him the words that he would not make peace so long as a single armed enemy remained on Russian soil and told him to transmit those words to Napoleon. Alexander did not insert them in his letter to Napoleon, because with his characteristic tact he felt it would be injudicious to use them at a moment when a last attempt at reconciliation was being made, but he definitely instructed Balashëv to repeat them personally to Napoleon.

cases.sentence: Отправляя Балашева, государь вновь повторил ему слова о том, что он не помирится до тех пор, пока останется хотя один вооруженный неприятель на ___, и приказал непременно передать эти слова Наполеону.
cases.explain: «русской земле» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: At two in the morning of the fourteenth of June, the Emperor, having sent for Balashëv and read him his letter to Napoleon, ordered him to take it and hand it personally to the French Emperor. When dispatching Balashëv, the Emperor repeated to him the words that he would not make peace so long as a single armed enemy remained on Russian soil and told him to transmit those words to Napoleon. Alexander did not insert them in his letter to Napoleon, because with his characteristic tact he felt it would be injudicious to use them at a moment when a last attempt at reconciliation was being made, but he definitely instructed Balashëv to repeat them personally to Napoleon.

cases.sentence: Выехав в ночь с 13-го на 14-е, Балашев, сопутствуемый трубачом и двумя казаками, к рассвету приехал в деревню Рыконты на ___ по сю сторону Немана.
cases.explain: «французские аванпосты» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Having set off in the small hours of the fourteenth, accompanied by a bugler and two Cossacks, Balashëv reached the French outposts at the village of Rykónty, on the Russian side of the Niemen, by dawn. There he was stopped by French cavalry sentinels.

cases.sentence: Французский ___, в малиновом мундире и мохнатой шапке, крикнул на подъезжавшего Балашева, приказывая ему остановиться.
cases.explain: «гусарский унтер-офицер» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A French noncommissioned officer of hussars, in crimson uniform and a shaggy cap, shouted to the approaching Balashëv to halt. Balashëv did not do so at once, but continued to advance along the road at a walking pace.

cases.sentence: Унтер-офицер, нахмурившись и проворчав какое-то ругательство, надвинулся грудью лошади на Балашева, взялся за саблю и грубо крикнул на ___, спрашивая его: глух ли он, что не слышит того, что̀ ему говорят.
cases.explain: «русского генерала» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The noncommissioned officer frowned and, muttering words of abuse, advanced his horse’s chest against Balashëv, put his hand to his saber, and shouted rudely at the Russian general, asking: was he deaf that he did not do as he was told? Balashëv mentioned who he was. The noncommissioned officer began talking with his comrades about regimental matters without looking at the Russian general.

cases.sentence: ___ и трубач и французские гусары молча изредка глядели друг на друга.
cases.explain: «Русские казаки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Balashëv looked around him, awaiting the arrival of an officer from the village. The Russian Cossacks and bugler and the French hussars looked silently at one another from time to time.

cases.sentence: Французский ___, видимо только что с постели, выехал из деревни на красивой, сытой, серой лошади, сопутствуемый двумя гусарами.
cases.explain: «гусарский полковник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: A French colonel of hussars, who had evidently just left his bed, came riding from the village on a handsome sleek gray horse, accompanied by two hussars. The officer, the soldiers, and their horses all looked smart and well kept.

cases.sentence: Они проехали деревню Рыконты мимо французских ___, часовых и солдат, отдававших честь своему полковнику и с любопытством осматривавших русский мундир, и выехали на другую сторону села.
cases.explain: «гусарских коновязей» — after the preposition «мимо», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: They rode through the village of Rykónty, past tethered French hussar horses, past sentinels and men who saluted their colonel and stared with curiosity at a Russian uniform, and came out at the other end of the village. The colonel said that the commander of the division was a mile and a quarter away and would receive Balashëv and conduct him to his destination.

cases.sentence: Солнце уже поднялось и весело блестело на ___.
cases.explain: «яркой зелени» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The sun had by now risen and shone gaily on the bright verdure.

cases.sentence: Человек этот поехал галопом навстречу Балашеву, блестя и развеваясь на ярком ___ своими перьями, каменьями и золотыми галунами.
cases.explain: «июньском солнце» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: They had hardly ridden up a hill, past a tavern, before they saw a group of horsemen coming toward them. In front of the group, on a black horse with trappings that glittered in the sun, rode a tall man with plumes in his hat and black hair curling down to his shoulders. He wore a red mantle, and stretched his long legs forward in French fashion. This man rode toward Balashëv at a gallop, his plumes flowing and his gems and gold lace glittering in the bright June sunshine.
